metadata.title: OpenAI, Anthropic are 'gambling with our lives': Fmr. employee warns of AI's threat to humanity

content.text:
A former Anthropic employee stated on X on Tuesday that both Anthropic and OpenAI are "not acting responsibly" and are "gambling with our lives." He also noted that many people building AI technology believe it could kill humanity in the next decade.
Sherwood News head of markets Luke Kawa and Investopedia editor in chief Caleb Silver discuss the details with Morning Brief host Julie Hyman.
There's another guy from Anthropic who who or from the AI world, an AI native, who now says, I resigned from Anthropic because we're developing technology that has the potential to end humanity. And we know that this is something that's been out there and then some of the other people from the company and from the community chime in and say there's a greater than 10% chance. Yes, that this happens.
I think the the proof's in the pudding. Who have they convinced that this is dangerous? Well, they've they've convinced governments this is dangerous and importantly, I think they've convinced the entire corporate world and investors that this is dangerous. Crowdstrike does not trade at a PE north of 140, and Palo Alto Networks does not trade at a PE around 80, unless people are very concerned about cyber security and the need for the spending on this to ramp up as you're deploying more agents.
But by the same token, they haven't convinced governments that it's dangerous. By and large, governments are not doing anything to curb the development of this technology.
No, they're betting it and they're greasing the skids here especially here in the United States for more build out because somebody has got to control this. But we don't know what they're ultimately trying to control and when the scientists are scared, we should probably be pretty scared too. This is just the latest scientist to say, I don't want any part of this. This has gone too far. We keep hearing more and more stories like that. And then we heard that story the other day that the Times came out with about how literally it had taken over itself. and now software is eating the world and when the scientists start quitting and say we don't want any part of it. even saw Sam Altman saying we need to take a pause here. I think the rest of us should think twice.
And as you say, companies are maybe they're scared of the hacking part of it. They don't seem scared about the super intelligence potential of it, right? Because they're they're spending on not this, you know, not that level of it. They're spending
That's the feature, not the bug, right? Like uh yeah, no, they're any anything but scared and like, hey, call me call me a cynic, but uh do I think we have you know, super intelligence deployed in uh robots before we have a very robust legal and regulatory framework over how even it's being used in in generative AI spaces today? Yeah, I'll I'll definitely go with the the more cynical answer on that.
I I do think though, to your point, it's uh, it's difficult to see how governments are wrestling with this. Hey, when you even have Texas and Pennsylvania, uh which you know, a relatively purple state and a more traditionally red state, that are kind of throwing up more guard rails around the development. Like the the biggest things that are kind of standing in the way of AI development right now seem to be access to resources and access to money and you know, I I think that does have a chance to potentially let the rest of us catch up. However, I'm not sure whether, you know, uh as we frame this continuously in terms of being an arms race, US and the rest of the world, particularly China. I'm not sure whether that outcome is indeed an optimal one to be aiming for either.
In terms of regulation, don't forget there weren't traffic lights and highways until there was a lot of fatalities with the introduction of the automobile.
Well, that's cheery. Thanks a lot, Caleb.
So sometimes it takes this to this technology to run its course and a lot of bad things to happen before you reel it in. Hopefully it won't get that bad, but seemed to be heading in that direction.
